q-171015.name: Question 1
q-171015.problem:
$\,$ $5>3$ and $7$ is even.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
q-171015.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law posits that the negation of a conjunction of two statements is equivalent to the disjunction of the negated individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows.

$$
¬(A∧B)=¬A∨¬B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(5>3\text{ and }7\text{ is even}) & ≡¬((5>3)∧(7\text{ is even})) \\  & ≡¬(5>3)∨¬(7\text{ is even}) \\  & ≡(5\le 3)∨(7\text{ is odd}) \\  & ≡5\le 3\text{ or }7\text{ is odd}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-171018.html:
Question 3
?

5 is prime and {5} is not empty.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?

a
5 is not prime and {5} is not empty
b
5 is not prime and {5} is empty
c
5 is prime or {5} is not empty
d
5 is not prime or {5} is not empty
e
5 is not prime or {5} is empty
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

De Morgan's law posits that the negation of a conjunction of two statements is equivalent to the disjunction of the negated individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows.

¬(A∧B)=¬A∨¬B

So, the negation of our statement is

¬(5 is prime and {5} is not empty)≡¬((5 is prime)∧({5} is not empty))≡¬(5 is prime)∨¬({5} is not empty)≡(5 is not prime)∨({5} is empty)≡5 is not prime or {5} is empty.

De Morgan's law posits that the negation of a conjunction of two statements is equivalent to the disjunction of the negated individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows.

$$
